title: memory/candidates/<id>.json (one candidate record) and memory/candidates/audit.jsonl (one audit row) — a candidate memory
description: ⛔ A CANDIDATE IS NOT A FACT. `verificationState` is the wall: only a `verified` record may be promoted to canonical project memory (memory/graph/<type>/<slug>.md, per memory/knowledge-graph.md's file-backed schema), promotion requires at least one supporting evidence path, and a `candidate` may only ever be recalled as an unverified lead. ONE FAMILY COVERS BOTH SHAPES (a candidate record and an audit-journal row) because they are the two faces of one mechanism and this registry names artifacts, not files — the same reasoning rollover-journal already uses for its row/snapshot pair. The two branches are INLINED rather than $ref'd via $defs (unlike rollover-journal) so this schema's own `schemaVersion` stays reachable by kernel/schema.test.mjs's version-authority fence, which walks oneOf/anyOf/allOf but not named $defs entries. TRACKED, not runtime: candidates are project knowledge-in-waiting (W5), evaluated and promoted or rejected by an explicit, audited human/agent decision — the opposite durability from the machine-local rollover handoff. The RECORD branch is copied from core/memory/candidate-memory.schema.json (core/ keeps its own normative copy for the same document, and the two are kept structurally identical — required fields, property types, enums — rather than one deferring to a path the other cannot resolve, since registry entries resolve schema files under schemas/ and core/ may not require anything outside itself); W6a converged the two copies' PROSE as well, so neither describes a layout the other contradicts. The store's directory belongs to the caller: core/memory/candidates.js appends a `memory` leaf to a conversation directory by default and takes an exact directory via `storeDir({dir})`, which is how kernel/respawnpack.js places this project-wide store at memory/candidates/ instead of inheriting a runtime caller's leaf.

oneOf.description: memory/candidates/<id>.json, as JSON.parse'd. Written by core/memory/candidates.js capture()/promote()/reject(); read by kernel/respawnpack.js's `memory candidates` verb.

claim.description: The assertion, as captured. A memory with no assertion asserts nothing and cannot be checked.

klass.description: Only these four may ever become canonical. Anything else is a note, and notes do not become project truth.

cycleId.description: WHICH CONTEXT CYCLE produced it. Required: a memory outlives the cycle that made it, and one that cannot name that cycle cannot be audited against what was known then. For a kernel-CLI capture (savepoint has no rollover-machine cycle of its own), this is the git revision the candidate was captured at.

evidencePaths.description: Paths, never conclusions. An empty array is a real answer and is exactly what blocks promotion.

previousState.description: A VERIFIED memory may be rejected later; findings are overturned. The prior state is kept so the audit shows what was believed and for how long.

oneOf.description: One line of memory/candidates/audit.jsonl, as JSON.parse'd. Written by core/memory/candidates.js's appendAudit() — every store mutation (capture/promote/reject) and every idempotent retry (promote-noop/reject-noop) and every refusal (promote-refused) appends one row, never rewritten. `id` and `by` are shared by every action; everything else is action-specific and left open, the same choice rollover-journal's row shape makes for the same reason: enumerating every action's fields here would either duplicate candidates.js's own field list beside a validator that cannot see it change, or force this schema to name a writer it does not describe.
